title: Failed RDMA teardown does not authorize freeing DMA buffers
applies_when: A native-resource leak or in-flight DMA hypothesis relies on a partial-construction early return, a transport close method, or cleanup after QP destruction or memory-region deregistration fails. Trace the owning factory, caller drain, destructor, retirement/retry path and buffer dependencies.
lesson: Distinguish acquisition failure from release failure. Mooncake's FIFO/SIEVE factories hold the new endpoint in a local shared_ptr and return nullptr on construct failure before publishing it; the destructor visits partially created non-null QPs and deletes work-depth state after successful teardown. An early return inside construct alone therefore does not establish a factory-path leak. A failed release is different: a device reference may remain alive. Before freeing backing memory, establish successful deregistration or documented quiescence. closeNotification preserves failed QP/MR handles and returns before buffer reset; the destructor explicitly retains DMA buffers on teardown failure. finishDestroy waits for outstanding work and bounds teardown retries. Destroying independent ordinary QPs does not justify freeing their dependent state or notification buffers after failure. Inspect the owner before proposing rollback; test successful release, failed dependency release and a later successful retry separately. Likewise, vLLM's P2P manager calls wait-cancel and poll for up to three seconds before transport close, then deliberately forces immediate cancellation on timeout. Reading NixlTransport.close alone misses that caller drain. Check the exact backend/version, timeout branch and surviving buffer lifetime before changing the policy; a bounded drain is neither absent synchronization nor proof of safe forced teardown.
avoid_when: This is source evidence only: no native RDMA failure-injection result, hardware quiescence or general leak-free claim. A caller retaining or directly retrying a partially constructed object requires separate analysis; the factory result does not cover it. finishDestroy can give up after bounded retries and log a possible leak. Reclaiming an independent resource may be safe after proving its lifetime; send-MR failure alone does not prove recv-MR deregistration must be skipped. Reopen with a supported path, resource dependency and safe reclaim guarantee. A mock observing another cleanup call does not establish hardware quiescence. Mocked NIXL unit tests cannot establish that deregistration or agent destruction stops residual DMA after the shutdown timeout. Do not replace a deliberate shutdown bound with an indefinite wait without a supported liveness contract; neither timeout safety nor a defect is established here.

evidence.note: The destructor deliberately releases owning smart pointers without deleting the DMA buffers after deconstructLocked fails; it documents the safety boundary. Source inspection only.
Outstanding-work checks precede teardown; failures retry up to a bound, then log a possible resource leak and retire. Not every provider failure is recoverable.
Notification teardown clears successful handles but returns on failed QP destruction or MR deregistration before resetting backing buffers.

FIFO local shared_ptr owns the endpoint during construct and unwinds on failure before map insertion. SIEVE has the same sequence at lines 240-253. Source ownership, not a verbs resource-count experiment.
Partial qp_list entries are null-skipped; successful destroys clear handles. Work-depth state is deleted only after all QP destroys succeed. Construction failure and destruction failure are distinct.

shutdown drains before session/control/data close. The best-effort loop uses the three-second constant at line 67, then deliberately forces immediate cancellation; source evidence does not prove residual DMA quiescence.

Transport close releases handles and deregisters memory before dropping the agent. Interpret this with the manager's drain and the actual native backend/version, not as a standalone proof of a missing wait or unsafe buffer reuse.
